answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to post a refundable stake before trading, like a quill signing a bond in ivory ink: the stake is locked, not spent, and slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicate accounts. A newcomer starts with a small trust dune of low-value trades, earning larger limits only after a history of honest deals. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs thousands of locked stakes, while honest agents get theirs back, so the attack becomes expensive and unprofitable.
